explanation: Default function arguments in C++ allow you to specify default values for parameters in a function declaration, making functions more flexible and user-friendly in real-world scenarios. This technique is particularly useful for optional parameters, such as configuration settings or fallback values, reducing the need for overloaded functions and improving code readability. Best practices include using defaults only for truly optional parameters, ensuring they are placed at the end of the parameter list (as required by C++), and avoiding defaults that could lead to subtle bugs, like unintended side effects or ambiguity in function overloading. Common pitfalls include forgetting that default values are evaluated at the point of declaration (not definition), which can cause issues in multi-file projects if headers are not managed carefully; to avoid this, always declare defaults in header files and test thoroughly. In real-world usage, this pattern is common in libraries and APIs, such as setting default timeouts in network functions or default sizes in data structures, promoting idiomatic C++ code that is both efficient and maintainable.
